style_when: the article is a purely conceptual synthesis or policy dilemma where no physical facility, machine, or supply chain exists, and an elegant abstract paper silhouette states the idea. Never reach for paper collage when the story describes physical manufacturing, freight, energy, hardware, or heavy infrastructure — use cinematic still or telephoto industry instead
prompt: Editorial cut-paper collage diptych arranged on a brushed-steel console desk in a control room. A torn vertical seam splits the frame: on the left, a crisp vendor software box with a wax-stamped renewal invoice and a hanging blank price tag, cut from slate-grey and bone-white rag paper; on the right, a half-assembled mechanism silhouette — flat-packed modules, gear wheels and a spanner fanned out in copper and graphite paper, one loose gear resting on the seam. Hand-torn fibre edges, halftone newsprint texture, physical cast shadows beneath every layer. A single raking key light from the left, muted slate, bone and copper palette, generous negative space, 16:9 split-screen diptych framing.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, legible print
rationale: Build vs buy is a pure procurement dilemma with no facility, machine or supply chain to photograph — exactly the case the collage catalogue names, and the desk rules explicitly list 'build vs buy' as a split-screen duality. Cut-paper silhouettes make both scenarios instantly nameable at card size while keeping the B2B register, and the treatment avoids repeating the last four headers.
cue: price the build like a renewal
subject: a split-paper diptych of a sealed vendor software box with a renewal invoice versus a half-assembled mechanism of parts
core_thesis: The first measured cohort of the AI build-vs-buy reset logged 26 in-house builds in two weeks and 23 report no saving at all, with zero verified payback reports — so the shift to building is real, the savings case is not, and a build must be priced with the same scrutiny as a renewal bill before committing.
core_conflict: The pull of cheap AI-assisted building against the unverified promise of savings — build-it-yourself momentum colliding with the disciplined arithmetic of the yearly vendor renewal.
composition: split-screen diptych with a torn vertical seam — vendor box and invoice on the left, sprawling half-built mechanism on the right, one loose gear resting on the seam
